questions.q: The degree of d³y/dx³ + 3(dy/dx)² = y² log(d²y/dx²) is —
questions.work: A derivative appears inside log, so the equation is not a polynomial in the derivatives: degree not defined.
Divide by x² − 1: P = 2x/(x² − 1). ∫P dx = log(x² − 1) ⇒ IF = x² − 1.
Highest derivative is d²y/dx², with power 2.
Highest order is 2; its highest power is 3.

questions.q: The integrating factor of dy/dx + 4y/x = 1/x is —
questions.work: P = 4/x ⇒ ∫P dx = 4 log x ⇒ IF = x⁴.

sections.title: Objective type questions of two 1-mark parts.

questions.q: (a) The distance between r·(i + j − k) + 4 = 0 and r·(i + j − k) + 5 = 0 is ______. (b) The order of y = dy/dx + (dy/dx)⁻¹ is ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) If y = √(sin³x), dy/dx = ______. (b) The order of x dx + y dy = 0 is ______.

sections.title: Objective type questions of four 1-mark parts.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The degree of (d²y/dx²)^(1/3) = x is ______. (ii) The differential equation with solution y = a cos x + b sin x is ______. (iii) The solution of dy/dx = e^(x+y) is e^y = ______. (iv) The number of arbitrary constants in a particular solution of a third-order equation is ______.
questions.answer:
(i) Cube both sides: d²y/dx² = x³ ⇒ degree 1.
(ii) y' = −a sin x + b cos x, y'' = −a cos x − b sin x = −y ⇒ y'' + y = 0.
(iii) e^(−y)dy = eˣdx ⇒ −e^(−y) = eˣ + C ⇒ e^y = −1/(eˣ + C).
(iv) 0.

dy/dx + (2/x)y = x. IF = e^(∫2/x dx) = x².
yx² = ∫x·x² dx = x⁴/4 + C ⇒ y = x²/4 + C/x².

questions.q: Find the general solution of log(dy/dx) = 2x + y.
Solve sec²y(1 + x²)dy + 2x tan y dx = 0, given y = π/4 when x = 1.
questions.answer:
Separate: sec²y/tan y dy = −2x/(1 + x²) dx.
log|tan y| = −log(1 + x²) + log C ⇒ tan y (1 + x²) = C.
At x = 1, y = π/4: 1 × 2 = C ⇒ (1 + x²)tan y = 2.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx + y cot x = 2 cos x.
questions.answer:
IF = e^(∫cot x dx) = sin x.
y sin x = ∫2 cos x sin x dx = ∫sin 2x dx = −cos 2x/2 + C.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = sin(x + y) + sin(x − y).
questions.answer:
sin(x + y) + sin(x − y) = 2 sin x cos y.
Separate: sec y dy = 2 sin x dx.
Integrate: log|sec y + tan y| = −2 cos x + C, i.e. log|sec y + tan y| + 2 cos x = C.
